difference_rationale: 50 ms is 10% of the existing 500 ms latency requirement. It is a declared operational resolution for this exploratory comparison, not a universal constant, significance test, equivalence proof, or campaign success criterion. All unrounded paired differences and error fractions are retained.
blocking: One runner per target/repetition, with all three paths sequentially executed on fresh stacks and volumes. Each of the six path permutations occurs once per target; their assignment to repetition IDs is fixed by SHA256 order_salt. Windows within a path and paths within a runner are dependent observations.
timing: Apply the initial allocation before load. At 180 seconds from the actual checkout scenario origin, update checkout and ad to the shared endpoint, reducing the donor first. The control performs two no-op quota updates at the same age. Record actual update times. Post-transition cohorts start at age 190 seconds, then every 60 seconds through age 490. The 180-190 second transition interval is retained separately. Never restart the stack or stop load at the endpoint.
quality: All initial, endpoint and final quotas including ad and memory must match. CPU period stays 100000 us. Same constant 40/s checkout and 100/s advertising streams throughout every path. Missing primary data or failed generator is infrastructure-invalid; completed load/timing mismatches retain outcomes but do not enter matched controlled contrasts. Restart/OOM remains diagnostic, not an exclusion or replacement SLO label.
analysis: Rescore retained events. Within each runner, compare decrease-control, recover-control, and decrease-recover in each aligned post-transition cohort. Report signed p95 differences, absolute difference relative to 50 ms, error fractions, SLO labels, actual rates, outstanding operations and failure diagnostics. Summarize paired differences by target and time without pooling repeated windows as independent runners. Similar last windows do not prove stationarity or establish a universal settling time.
timeouts: Completed failed and timed-out HTTP requests remain in descriptive SLO p95; unsuccessful operations remain in error fractions. Preserve status and timeout diagnostics. A client deadline is not a measured successful server completion time; do not fit such observations as exact successful latencies or remove them to fit only successes. No response-time model is fitted here.
scope: History dependence of the measured checkout requirement at two complete endpoint allocations. The recovery path deliberately starts in an overloaded regime; it is not a safe adaptation policy. This is not a validated boundary model, step-to-boundary estimate, or coordinate-system comparison.
retry: Only infrastructure-failed blocks may be rerun, with all three paths repeated on the replacement runner. Use the latest whole block attempt regardless of outcomes and retain attempt statuses; never combine paths from different attempts or retry SLO failures.
